method: Every finding re-run against the live audit/release-1.0-2026-07 working tree with /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python, MPLBACKEND=Agg. Doc findings checked against current docstrings/source. X3 timing claims re-measured only where cheap (gif frame delays); 46s-animation and 59s-align timings judged by code inspection, marked not re-measured.

verdicts.note: Behavioral half FIXED: align(single 2D array) now returns a bare ndarray and the Returns doc describes exactly that ('a single bare array/DataFrame returns a single array'). RESIDUE: the parenthetical '(matching hyp.reduce/hyp.cluster/hyp.manip, and the classic hyp.align API, which have always returned arrays)' still lumps manip in 'returned arrays' while manip demonstrably returns DataFrames (verified type(hyp.manip(A)) == DataFrame). Cosmetic doc residue only.

Divergence persists behaviorally (reduce([A])/normalize([A]) -> ndarray; align([A])/manip([A]) -> list[1]) but is now explicitly documented in each direction: reduce Returns says 'a single dataset -- even inside a one-element list -- comes back as a bare array'; align Returns says 'a list input returns a list'. The fix waves chose documented per-function conventions over unification.

Split persists (manip/impute/predict -> DataFrame; reduce/normalize -> ndarray; verified) but manip's docstring now carries an explicit Notes block documenting the DataFrame-vs-array conventions (index preservation, NaN propagation, ddof, 1-D orientation). Documented deliberate design, addressing the finding's docs_impact.

PARTIAL: model= is now accepted as an alias on reduce/normalize/cluster (hyp.reduce(A, model='PCA') and hyp.cluster(A, model='KMeans') work), closing the spec-kwarg half. RESIDUE: data-arg naming still split -- hyp.plot(data=A) -> TypeError "missing a required argument: 'x'"; hyp.manip(x=A) -> TypeError missing 'data'.

hyp.reduce(A, reduce='NotAModel') now raises "unknown reduce model 'NotAModel'; supported names: Autoencoder, BayesianGaussianMixture, ..." -- modern sibling-matching grammar, no whitespace runs, no legacy URL.

All entry points now reject []: reduce/manip/cluster 'input has no observations (0 rows)'; align/predict/impute/analyze 'input has no observations (got an empty list); there is nothing to align/forecast/impute/analyze'. No text-corpus load; analyze([]) no longer returns [] silently.

Unknown kwargs now raise: align SRM bogus kwarg -> TypeError 'SharedResponseModel() got unexpected keyword argument(s)... Supported: features'; predict -> TypeError from Kalman.__init__; impute PPCA -> TypeError. The dangerous silent random_state=N case now raises the same TypeError (verified).

Signature census unchanged: random_state only on plot/analyze/reduce/cluster; align/manip/predict/impute/apply_model still have none. Mitigation since filing: a passed random_state now raises TypeError instead of being silently ignored, so users are no longer deceived -- but there is still no public seed path for SRM/stochastic imputers.

save() is now def save(obj, fname, protocol=None) with a full extension-aware docstring; unknown kwargs raise TypeError ('unexpected keyword argument bogus'); protocol=999 raises HypertoolsIOError instead of being dropped.

max_dims now documented as EXCLUSIVE ('Dimensionalities 2 through max_dims - 1... the bound is EXCLUSIVE, matching Python's range') with UserWarning on clamping; the unconditional slow-warning is gone (verified 0 warnings on 50x8 describe); 'average' remains the stacked-all-data curve, which matches its documented description 'for all data', and is now drawn on the figure.
load() docstring now reads 'spiral is a list of two (1000, 3) numpy arrays containing 3D spiral data' -- matches verified behavior (list of two (1000,3) arrays).

Verbatim: hypertools still defines no __all__; from hypertools import * still exposes config/core/datageometry/external/tools; hypertools.config.version is still the raw importlib.metadata.version function object. Unchanged.

PARTIAL: Pipeline('ZScore') now raises the requested clear TypeError ('steps must be a list of step specs, got str... e.g. Pipeline([ZScore, PCA])'). RESIDUE: hyp.apply_model(A, ['ZScore', {...}]) still raises "unknown model 'ZScore'; supported names: AffinityPropagation, ..." -- the apply_model list-pipeline registry still excludes manip/align/predict/impute names that hypertools.Pipeline resolves.

Verbatim repro: hyp.predict(traj, model='Kalman', t=25) -> (25,3) while plot(..., predict='Kalman', t=25, return_model=True) bundle forecast -> (26,3) with params {'t': 25}; return_model doc still promises 'forecasts t new rows' with no mention of the prepended seam row.
hyp.reduce(randn(30,5), ndims=10) now emits UserWarning 'ndims/n_components was set to 10 but the data only has 5 feature(s), so no reduction was performed...' while returning (30,5).

PARTIAL: MDS half FIXED -- hyp.reduce(x,'MDS') now runs with zero FutureWarnings (defaults pinned). RESIDUE: every hyp.manip list call still emits Pandas4Warning 'The copy keyword is deprecated...' from datawrangler/decorate/decorate.py:421 (upstream pydata-wrangler; same residue as X4-002).

matplotlib describe figure now draws one distinguishable color per dataset plus the 'average' curve with a legend (verified: labels ['dataset 0','dataset 1','dataset 2','average'], 4 distinct colors, legend present) -- matching the plotly encoding as the updated docstring promises.

Verbatim: hyp.align([X,Y], model='hyper') emits no DeprecationWarning (recorded list empty under simplefilter('always')), while the docstring still calls 'hyper' a deprecated alias and the align= kwarg path does warn.

All four rough edges fixed: 3D input -> 'each dataset must be a 2-D (observations x features) array; dataset 0 has 3 dimensions (shape (2, 30, 5))'; hyp.align((A,B)) tuple now works (returns list); hyp.load(12345) -> 'hypertools.load: dataset must be a string (a dataset name, file path, or URL)...'; pipeline='x' -> 'pipeline= expects a fitted hypertools.Pipeline (e.g. the model returned by analyze(..., return_model=True))'.

PARTIAL: set_interactive_backend('NotABackend') now raises ValueError naming valid options (fixed). RESIDUE: hyp.cluster(A) still returns a plain Python list of numpy int32 scalars (verified list/int32), the only per-observation API result without ndarray form.

kernel_width=-5 now raises ValueError 'kernel_width must be a positive odd integer; got -5' (no AssertionError); kernel_width=10 warns 'Increasing smoothing kernel width by 1 (must be odd)'; 4.5 warns 'Rounding... to the nearest integer'; 0 coerces with an explicit warning before the savgol check. Contract now accurate and coercions audible.

model=42 now raises ValueError from every dispatcher: reduce 'invalid reduce model 42 (type int): a reduce spec must be...'; cluster 'invalid cluster model 42 (type int): it has no fit or fit_predict method. Pass one of the supported...' (no more AttributeError mid-fit); align 'unknown model spec: got a int instance... Pass one of D...'. Consistent class, each message names the value, type, and remedies.
Same fix as X1-007: reduce unknown-model error now enumerates supported names, no embedded whitespace, no legacy readthedocs URL.

Verbatim: hyp.cluster(X, n_clusters=0) still raises sklearn.utils._param_validation.InvalidParameterError ("The 'n_clusters' parameter of KMeans must be an int in the range [1, inf). Got 0 instead."). Note: InvalidParameterError subclasses ValueError, so except ValueError does catch it -- the finding's 'cannot catch a stable builtin class' claim overstates; residue is the leaked private class name only.

PARTIAL: static plot with duration=-5 no longer crashes (static rendering decoupled from animation kwargs -- F01-007). RESIDUE: rotations='two' still accepted at plot() time and dies at save with bare IndexError 'list index out of range' deep in matplotlib; zoom=-1 still silently accepted.

PARTIAL: ax='myaxis' -> TypeError 'ax= must be a matplotlib Axes (2-D) or Axes3D (3-D) instance; got str'; size=[4,4,4] -> ValueError naming size; hue 3-D -> TypeError explaining accepted hue forms; unknown kwargs (morph_samples path) rejected eagerly. RESIDUE: transform='banana' still AttributeError "'str' object has no attribute 'shape'"; fmt=123 still TypeError "object of type 'int' has no len()".

PARTIAL: the headline case is fixed -- labels=['only-label'] on 20 points now raises ValueError 'labels has 1 entry but the data has 20 observations; labels must have exactly one entry per observation...'. RESIDUE: hue='notacolumn' (bare string, undocumented form) and legend=7 are still silently accepted.

Verbatim: describe max_dims=0/-3 and 1-column data still return {'average': [], 'individual': [[]]} silently; max_dims=2.5 still bare TypeError "'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer"; backend='bogus' still unvalidated when show=False. (The unconditional slow-warning is gone.)

PARTIAL: reduce(X, 'PCA', ndims=10) now warns 'ndims/n_components was set to 10 but the data only has 4 feature(s)...' (cap made audible). RESIDUE: hyp.apply_model(X, 'PCA', ndims=0) still silently returns a (20, 0) array while reduce(ndims=0) raises.
Verbatim: hyp.align([X,Y], model='SRM', features=-1) still raises ValueError 'negative dimensions are not allowed' from numpy internals, never naming features.
hyp.predict(rand(1,4), t=5) now raises ValueError 'cannot forecast from a single observation: the dataset has only 1 row. Forecasting needs at least 2 observations (rows)...'.

hyp.load(123) and hyp.load(None) now raise 'hypertools.load: dataset must be a string (a dataset name, file path, or URL), a path-like object, or a list/tuple...' -- the contract-naming message the finding requested.

hyp.save(X, 42) now raises TypeError 'hypertools.save: fname must be a string or path-like object, got int. Did you swap the argument order?...' (no fd write risk); unpicklable objects raise HypertoolsIOError 'could not pickle function object for saving to ...' with context; docstring is now a full extension-aware numpydoc.
hyp.impute(np.full((10,3), np.nan)) now raises ValueError 'input is entirely missing (all values are NaN); there is nothing to impute from.'
load() docstring corrected: spiral described as 'a list of two (1000, 3) numpy arrays'; mushrooms text now reads '8,124 mushroom samples' (typo gone).

hyp.analyze(None) -> TypeError 'Unsupported data type passed to analyze: None. Supported types: ...'; hyp.analyze([]) -> ValueError 'input has no observations (got an empty list)'; pipeline='x' -> TypeError 'pipeline= expects a fitted hypertools.Pipeline...'.

Pipeline('PCA') -> TypeError 'steps must be a list of step specs, got str (PCA); e.g. Pipeline([ZScore, PCA])...'; Pipeline([42]) now fails EAGERLY ('pipeline step 42 resolved to a int, which has no fit/fit_transform/... method'); Pipeline(None) -> same clear steps-must-be-a-list TypeError.

Static line plots are no longer lossy: 10,000-sample repro now draws all 10,000 vertices (was 900), so the spike sample is drawn and the endpoint is included (interp rewrite has exact endpoints per F04-004; static density fixed as _STATIC_LINE_TARGET_VERTICES upsampling-only, F01-007). Verified fig.axes[0].lines[0] X.shape == (10000,).

duration/frame_rate no longer reshape static plots: duration=60,frame_rate=30 and duration=1,frame_rate=2 both draw all 10,000 vertices (was 1800 / 2). Docstrings updated: 'Has no effect on static plots (static line smoothing uses a fixed density, independent of the animation kwargs)'.

Verbatim: hyp.align([<(2,100,3)>, <(2,100,3)>]) and hyp.align(bare 3D array) are still silently accepted and flattened -- out[0].shape == (2, 300), no error/warning. (reduce, by contrast, now rejects 3D with a clear message.) 59s slow-variant timing not re-measured; the flattening path is unchanged so it stands.
Same fix as X1-007/X2-011: reduce unknown-model error now lists supported names with clean formatting and no stale URL.

New _RealTimePillowWriter cumulatively rounds per-frame delays onto the GIF centisecond grid (code cites this audit, F04-010). Measured: duration=2, frame_rate=30 gif -> 60 frames, delays alternating 30/40 ms, total exactly 2000 ms.

Defaults unchanged (duration=30 x frame_rate=30 = 900 frames on animate=True export); no cost caveat in the save_path/duration docstrings and no progress indicator (grep: no tqdm/progress in plot.py/animate.py). 46s/19.7MB timing not re-measured; frame count driving it is unchanged. Enhancement-level residue.

plot() ndims docstring rewritten: 'If ndims > 3, the data is analyzed at that dimensionality but plotted in 3 dimensions (a second, display-only reduction...); use return_model=True to retrieve the higher-dimensional analyzed data.' Matches the 1.0 Figure return contract.

hyp.plot(x, bananas=7) now fails in ~0.00s BEFORE the pipeline with TypeError "plot() got an unexpected keyword argument 'bananas' (extra keyword arguments are passed through to matplotlib line artists...)" -- the eager pre-flight probe plus did-you-mean machinery is in the docstring and behavior.

Verbatim: hyp.manip([a,b],'ZScore') still emits Pandas4Warning 'The copy keyword is deprecated and will be removed in a future version...' from datawrangler/decorate/decorate.py:421. Upstream pydata-wrangler fix or pandas pin still needed; unchanged in hypertools' venv.
hyp.reduce(randn(60,10), 'MDS', ndims=3) now runs with ZERO warnings under simplefilter('always') -- n_init/init defaults evidently pinned in the MDS spec.
hyp.cluster(d, cluster='HDBSCAN') now runs with ZERO warnings under simplefilter('always') -- copy pinned.
hyp.describe(randn(30,5)) emits no 'When input data is large...' warning (0 warnings recorded). The unconditional warn call is gone.

hyp.describe(randn(30,5), show=True) under MPLBACKEND=Agg emits no 'FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive' warning (0 warnings recorded); describe now follows plot()'s display convention and returns the fig in the result dict.
hyp.load('sotus') now returns a plain list (raw data, not a fitted sklearn Pipeline) with ZERO InconsistentVersionWarnings -- payload path re-serialized per the 1.0 load() design.

Verbatim: hyp.plot(d, cluster={'model':'KMeans','params':{...}}) still attributes the legacy-dict DeprecationWarning to a library frame (now plot/backend.py:1332), so under Python's default filters plot()/analyze() users see nothing.

Re-run AST census (excluding externals): 104 warnings.warn call sites, 33 with stacklevel, 46 with explicit category -- the majority are still bare UserWarnings attributed to hypertools internals; no hypertools warning category class. Proportion improved but the inconsistency stands.

Auto fig.show() fires ONLY in plain non-interactive scripts and is a documented deliberate design (plotly_backend.py:1108-1118 explains notebook suppression and 'use show=False to hold the Figure'; the show docstring documents auto-suppression). The leaked-socket ResourceWarning is upstream plotly (_base_renderers.py open_html_in_browser); show=False verified clean by the original auditor. Not re-run here (would launch a browser).
Verbatim: first hyp.reduce(x, 'UMAP') still surfaces ImportWarning 'Tensorflow not installed; ParametricUMAP will be unavailable' from umap/__init__.py.
Verbatim: hyp.plot(d, animate=True); del ani; gc.collect() still emits matplotlib's 'Animation was deleted without rendering anything' UserWarning with no hypertools-idiomatic (save_path=) guidance.
Message rewritten: 'Cannot reduce a single observation (row) of data; returning a zero vector of length ndims instead. ...' -- grammatical and behavior-accurate.
The audit's own trap case now works: hyp.cluster(randn(40,5), model='KMeans') is accepted (model= aliases added to cluster/reduce/normalize), removing the cross-function transfer failure.

Verbatim: predict/arima.py:83-85 still wraps the statsmodels fit in catch_warnings with simplefilter('ignore', UserWarning) and simplefilter('ignore', convergence_warning); suppressed diagnostics are not collected or exposed. Enhancement-level residue.

22 consecutive hyp.plot() calls emit no 'More than 20 figures' RuntimeWarning and leave 0 figures in the pyplot registry (plt.get_fignums() == []) -- figure lifecycle fixed despite plt.figure() still appearing at 3 call sites.

Informational triage table, not a defect: it documents that remaining import-time warning-filter mutations are upstream (scipy/sklearn/requests/IPython) and that hypertools installs zero global filters. Nothing to fix or reproduce; its release-notes suggestion is editorial. No known-warnings docs section exists, but the finding's own 'expected' field is 'n/a (documentation of triage)'.
